acceptance.given: An aggregate evaluation has matrix evidence associated with a subject other than the subject being evaluated.

oracle.expected: The evaluation records the aggregate as invalid and does not admit it as valid.
forbidden: The aggregate is treated as valid despite wrong-target matrix evidence.
oracle.observable: The matrix replay receipt and aggregate decision identify the target mismatch and show an invalid aggregate status.

acceptance.when: The Toolchain matrix evaluator validates target bindings before deriving the aggregate verdict.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the wrong-target matrix-evidence scenario and require aggregate admission to fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Reject aggregate admission when any matrix receipt binds evidence to a subject other than the aggregate's evaluated subject.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Restoring the prior evaluator preserves existing matrix receipt formats and only removes the wrong-target invalidation rule.

slice_hint.state_transition: Matrix evidence with a mismatched target moves the aggregate from evaluating to invalid.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: A wrong-target matrix-evidence scenario produces an invalid aggregate decision and cannot produce a valid aggregate.

acceptance.given: Subjects, Probes, Matrix Cases, Consumers, and rollback stages participate in one evaluation and rollback workflow.

oracle.expected: The isolation-boundary check shows separate mutable state and evidence ownership for every listed component.
forbidden: Mutable state is shared between any of the listed components.
Shared mutable state allows one component's execution to alter another component's result.
oracle.observable: During the Toolchain case-evidence evaluation phase, component descriptors, evidence roots, and rollback state are checked for distinct ownership boundaries.

acceptance.then: Each listed component has isolated mutable state, so execution cannot cross-contaminate another component's result.
acceptance.when: The Toolchain evaluates component descriptors, evidence bindings, and rollback-stage state before publishing a result.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Exercise distinct component descriptors and reject any shared mutable-state or evidence ownership boundary.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Enforce distinct mutable-state and evidence ownership boundaries for subjects, probes, matrix cases, consumers, and rollback stages before evidence can establish success.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Restoring the prior ownership checks preserves descriptor and case-evidence schemas without sharing mutable state.

slice_hint.state_transition: The evaluation workflow moves from isolated component inputs to independently bound component evidence, or rejects a detected shared-state boundary.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The evaluation-phase boundary check establishes separate mutable-state and evidence ownership for every listed component; any shared boundary rejects success.

acceptance.given: A non-empty Consumer Manifest identifies repository callers with applicable route transitions and rollback behavior.

oracle.expected: Every Consumer Manifest entry completes every applicable route transition and, after rollback, observes the Prior Behavior Baseline; the manifest is reconciled bidirectionally with the repository real-call surface.
forbidden: Any manifest entry fails to complete an applicable route transition.
An applicable route transition is skipped or left incomplete for a manifest entry.
A Consumer Manifest omits a VDD, Acceptance, or workflow-model-routing real caller.
Rollback completes without observing the Prior Behavior Baseline for a manifest entry.
oracle.observable: The Toolchain consumer-route evaluation records each manifest entry, its applicable transitions, bidirectional reconciliation against VDD, Acceptance, and workflow-model-routing callers, and its post-rollback baseline observation.

acceptance.then: All applicable route transitions for every Consumer Manifest entry are complete and each entry observes the Prior Behavior Baseline after rollback.
acceptance.when: The Toolchain processes the non-empty Consumer Manifest, reconciles it with the repository real-call surface, executes applicable transitions, and evaluates rollback.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run a non-empty manifest scenario with an incomplete applicable transition or missing post-rollback baseline observation and require success admission to fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Require a complete non-empty Consumer Manifest to reconcile bidirectionally with the repository VDD, Acceptance, and workflow-model-routing real-call surface, complete every applicable transition, and observe the Prior Behavior Baseline after rollback.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Restoring the prior route evaluator preserves existing replay interfaces while removing Consumer Manifest transition and post-rollback baseline enforcement.

slice_hint.state_transition: Each manifest entry moves from pending applicable transitions to transition-complete with a post-rollback Prior Behavior Baseline observation, or the evaluation rejects success.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: 100% of non-empty Consumer Manifest entries reconcile bidirectionally to the repository real-call surface, complete every applicable transition, and observe the Prior Behavior Baseline after rollback.

acceptance.given: An invalid package is presented to the Toolchain package evaluator.

oracle.expected: The invalid-package evaluation returns a rejection and cannot be recorded as successful.
forbidden: Treating the invalid-package case as successful.
oracle.observable: The package replay result for the invalid package has a non-success outcome and the negative compatibility probe does not admit success.

acceptance.when: The Toolchain runs the invalid-package case through the configured package validator and negative compatibility probe.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the invalid-package matrix case and require its attempted success admission to fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Make invalid-package evaluation reject success, including when a validator would otherwise return success for the invalid package.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Restoring the prior package evaluator preserves its command-line interface and capability schema while removing invalid-package success rejection.

slice_hint.state_transition: An invalid package moves from submitted for evaluation to rejected, never to successful.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The invalid-package matrix case produces a rejection and cannot be admitted as success.
